## [v0.87.0](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/releases/tag/v0.87.0)
*GitHub Releases · Crush* | 24/07/2026 | Score: 0.70
Tags: mcp, product_launch, developer_tool, cli_tool, tool_update

> <h1>MCP OAuth, performance and more</h1> <p>Happy Friday everybody!</p> <p>We're releasing some nice features for you so you can enjoy your weekend vibecoding. (Or not, stay outside 🌞 and return to Crush on Monday! 😃).</p> <h2>MCP OAuth</h2> <p>That's it, it's finally here! Some of you have been asking for this for long.</p> <p>This is required for some MCPs to work. Want to know to it set it up? <a href="https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush#mcp-oauth">Refer to this section into the README</a>.</p> <p>Thank <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/joestump/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/joestump">@joestump</a> and his agent <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/joestump-agent/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/joestump-agent">@joestump-agent</a> for this contribution. And of course, our favorite <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/taciturnaxolotl/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/taciturnaxolotl">@taciturnaxolotl</a> also helped.</p> <h2>Claude Channels MCP extension</h2> <p><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/joestump/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/joestump">@joestump</a> (and his agent) <em>also</em> added an initial implementation to support the <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference" rel="nofollow">Claude Channels MCP extension</a>, which means MCPs can now send notifications to Crush when certain events happen.</p> <p>Give this a try if you're interested, and let us know how well it works for you.</p> <h2>Restored MCP prompts</h2> <p>MCP prompts were unintentionally disabled in a previous release, but they were now added back!</p> <h2>LSP performance boost</h2> <p>Another cool contrib was made by <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/TheJhyeFactor/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/TheJhyeFactor">@TheJhyeFactor</a>, who vastly improved the CPU and memory usage on handling LSP servers in large repositories!</p> <p>See <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="4922746509" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/issues/3370" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/charmbracelet/crush/pull/3370/hovercard" href="https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/pull/3370">#3370</a> for a more in-depth explanation of the optimizations.</p> <h2>Bang mode performance boost</h2> <p><a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/TheJhyeFactor/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/TheJhyeFactor">@TheJhyeFactor</a> <em>also</em> improved performance of output streaming when running command in bang mode.</p> <p>Check <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="4928375063" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/issues/3381" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/charmbracelet/crush/pull/3381/hovercard" href="https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/pull/3381">#3381</a> to see some benchmarking.</p> <h2><code>/etc/crush/crush.json</code></h2> <p>You read it right! Thank to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/Muttaqin86/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/Muttaqin86">@Muttaqin86</a> you can now have a system-wide Crush configuration on <code>/etc/crush/crush.json</code>.</p> <p>The motivation for this was improving compatibility with NixOS.</p> <h2>Fixed Copilot + GPT-5.6</h2> <p>All three GPT-5.6 models (Sol, Terra and Luna) are now fixed when running via GitHub Copilot. Kudos to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/nghiant03/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/nghiant03">@nghiant03</a> for this!</p> <p>That was a lot, but it's really fun to how much the community is enganged with Crush dev.</p> <p>Keep Crushing! ™️<br> Charm</p> ## [vercel@57.0.0](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/releases/tag/vercel%4057.0.0)
*GitHub Releases · Vercel CLI* | 24/07/2026 | Score: 0.70
Tags: api_update, developer_tool, cli_tool, tool_update

> <h3>Minor Changes</h3> <ul> <li><a class="commit-link" data-hovercard-type="commit" data-hovercard-url="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/7dd4301c6af9e93903244464ecd351abde3cae5d/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/7dd4301c6af9e93903244464ecd351abde3cae5d"><tt>7dd4301</tt></a>: Make service bindings type optional.</li> </ul> <h3>Patch Changes</h3> <ul> <li><a class="commit-link" data-hovercard-type="commit" data-hovercard-url="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/3a066fe3573b4df3e3c50fbd42d98e37ab532538/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/3a066fe3573b4df3e3c50fbd42d98e37ab532538"><tt>3a066fe</tt></a>: Add a <code>resolved</code> attribute to the <code>vc.importBuilders</code> trace span recording each Builder's resolved version and source directory</li> <li><a class="commit-link" data-hovercard-type="commit" data-hovercard-url="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/b40db5b665a9cfbe6be70dc38ad2f233b2209b06/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/b40db5b665a9cfbe6be70dc38ad2f233b2209b06"><tt>b40db5b</tt></a>: Improve <code>vc alerts</code> and <code>vc alerts rules</code> output for custom alerts, including readable inspect views, custom alert rule filtering, compact rule tables, and normalized alert timestamps.</li> <li><a class="commit-link" data-hovercard-type="commit" data-hovercard-url="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/fca6de2274fc0eb873a0253b40a5c02703e6bd82/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/fca6de2274fc0eb873a0253b40a5c02703e6bd82"><tt>fca6de2</tt></a>: Added a notice when a project's first <code>vercel deploy</code> (without <code>--prod</code>) is assigned to production by the API. The notice explains that this is expected behavior for the first deployment and that future deployments will be preview deployments unless <code>--prod</code> is used. ## [pnpm 12 Alpha 18](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.0.0-alpha.18)
*GitHub Releases · pnpm* | 22/07/2026 | Score: 0.70
Tags: github_release, developer_tool, cli_tool, tool_update

> <h2>Minor Changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p>The first release of a package now publishes the version written in its manifest verbatim, instead of bumping off it. <code>pnpm version -r</code> and <code>pnpm change status</code> check the registry for each release's current version; when that version is not yet published, the package debuts at it and its pending changesets apply only from the next release. A newly added package seeded at <code>1100.0.0</code> with a <code>minor</code> changeset is therefore published as <code>1100.0.0</code> rather than skipping straight to <code>1100.1.0</code>.</p> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm version</code> now supports the npm-style bump forms: <code>pnpm version <major|minor|patch|premajor|preminor|prepatch|prerelease></code> and <code>pnpm version <exact-version></code> (also recursively with <code>-r</code>), with <code>--preid</code>, <code>--allow-same-version</code>, <code>--message</code>, <code>--no-git-tag-version</code>, <code>--no-commit-hooks</code>, <code>--sign-git-tag</code>, <code>--tag-version-prefix</code>, and <code>--json</code>. The bump runs the <code>preversion</code>/<code>version</code>/<code>postversion</code> lifecycle scripts and records the new version as a git commit and tag.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added recursive workspace support to <code>pnpm outdated</code>. <code>pnpm list</code> and <code>pnpm ll</code> now inspect all workspace projects by default, matching the TypeScript CLI.</p> </li> <li> <p>Made recursive <code>pnpm rebuild</code> honor workspace filters with shared and dedicated lockfiles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Made <code>pnpm why</code> and <code>pnpm peers</code> recursive by default in workspaces. Recursive peer checks now honor workspace filters, and recursive <code>why</code> can inspect the active project when a workspace uses dedicated lockfiles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added a <code>--changeset</code> flag to <code>pnpm update</code>. Set <code>update.changeset</code> to <code>true</code> in <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code> to enable this behavior by default, and use <code>--no-changeset</code> to override the setting for one update. After the update completes, pnpm writes a <code>.changeset/pnpm-update-<suffix>.md</code> file declaring a patch bump for every workspace package whose <code>dependencies</code> or <code>optionalDependencies</code> were changed by the update and a major bump when <code>peerDependencies</code> changed, including packages that consume an updated catalog entry via the <code>catalog:</code> protocol. Private packages, packages without a name, and packages listed in the <code>ignore</code> array of <code>.changeset/config.json</code> are skipped. If <code>.changeset/config.json</code> does not exist, a warning is printed and no changeset is generated.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added GitHub Actions dependencies to <code>pnpm outdated</code> and interactive <code>pnpm update</code>. Non-interactive updates can include them with <code>--include-github-actions</code> or by setting <code>update.githubActions</code> to <code>true</code> in <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code>. Updated actions are pinned to exact commit hashes with their release tags preserved in comments.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Patch Changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Fixed <code>pnpm install</code> rewriting unrelated <code>pnpm-lock.yaml</code> entries after a small manifest change — for example, removing one dev dependency could bump other packages' open-range dependencies (such as jest's <code>@types/node: '*'</code>) to their newest versions <a href="https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13193" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13193/hovercard">pnpm/pnpm#13193</a>. Three resolution-reuse gaps caused still-satisfied lockfile entries to be re-resolved from the registry:</p> <ul> <li>Direct dependencies using the <code>catalog:</code> protocol were compared against the lockfile in their resolved-range form, so every catalog-managed dependency looked changed on every install, and any package depending on one was re-resolved.</li> <li>Auto-installed (hoisted) peer dependencies were also treated as changed direct dependencies on every install.</li> <li>When a package had to resolve freshly but landed on the version the lockfile already recorded, its dependency subtree was still re-resolved instead of being reused, drifting open ranges pinned by the lockfile.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm install</code>, <code>pnpm add</code>, <code>pnpm update</code>, and <code>pnpm remove</code> now support recursive (<code>-r</code>) and filtered (<code>--filter</code>) execution in workspaces configured with one lockfile per project (<code>sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false</code>), instead of failing with <code>ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_SHARED_LOCKFILE_UNSUPPORTED</code>. Each selected project is installed independently against its own <code>pnpm-lock.yaml</code>, <code>node_modules</code>, and virtual store, matching pnpm.</p> </li> <li> <p>Global commands (<code>pnpm add -g</code>, <code>pnpm runtime set -g</code>, ...) now create a missing global bin directory instead of failing with <code>ERR_PNPM_PNPM_DIR_NOT_WRITABLE</code>, and the universal <code>--silent</code> / <code>-s</code> shorthands for <code>--reporter=silent</code> (e.g. <code>pnpm store path --silent</code>) are supported again.</p> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm unlink</code> now reinstalls through the selection-aware install pipeline, matching pnpm: it honors <code>-r</code> / <code>--filter</code>, installs recursively by default inside a workspace, and supports both a shared workspace lockfile and one lockfile per project (<code>sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false</code>). Previously it always reinstalled only the active project.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added <code>update</code> and <code>audit</code> settings sections to <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code>, superseding the awkwardly named <code>updateConfig</code>, <code>auditConfig</code>, and top-level <code>auditLevel</code> settings:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="update: ignoreDeps: # was updateConfig.ignoreDependencies - webpack - "@babel/*" audit: level: high # was auditLevel ignore: # was auditConfig.ignoreGhsas - GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz"><pre><span class="pl-ent">update</span>: <span class="pl-ent">ignoreDeps</span>: <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was updateConfig.ignoreDependencies</span> - <span class="pl-s">webpack</span> - <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>@babel/*<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-ent">audit</span>: <span class="pl-ent">level</span>: <span class="pl-s">high </span><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was auditLevel</span> <span class="pl-ent">ignore</span>: <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was auditConfig.ignoreGhsas</span> - <span class="pl-s">GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz</span></pre></div> <p><code>update.ignoreDeps</code> lists dependency name patterns that <code>pnpm update</code> and <code>pnpm outdated</code> should skip. <code>audit.level</code> and <code>audit.ignore</code> tune <code>pnpm audit</code>.</p> <p>The deprecated <code>updateConfig</code>, <code>auditConfig</code>, and <code>auditLevel</code> settings keep working until the next major version. When both a new section value and its deprecated counterpart are set, the new section takes precedence and a warning is printed. Both the TypeScript CLI and the Rust config surface (pacquet) recognize the new sections.</p> </li> </ul>

> <h2>Patch Changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Close three CLI parity gaps with the TypeScript pnpm CLI:</p> <ul> <li><code>--registry <url></code> is now accepted on every command as a universal rc-option, not only through <code>--config.registry=<url></code> (<code>pnpm view pnpm dist-tags.latest --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/</code>).</li> <li><code>pnpm add</code> (and <code>pnpm add -g</code>) now accept <code>--allow-build=<pkg></code>, appending the named packages to <code>allowBuilds</code> so they can run their lifecycle scripts during the install (<code>pnpm add @pnpm/exe@11.16.0 --allow-build=@pnpm/exe</code>).</li> <li><code>--dir</code> / <code>-C</code> is now position-independent: it is accepted anywhere on the command line, before or after the subcommand (<code>pnpm add foo --dir /tmp/proj</code>).</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm publish --provenance</code> now applies the <code>fetch-timeout</code> setting to the sigstore signing exchange and retries it up to two more times with exponential backoff when it fails or times out, instead of aborting the publish on the first transient network error or hanging on a stalled connection.</p> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm update --latest</code> now resolves a dependency declared through an <code>npm:</code> alias — directly in <code>package.json</code> or in the catalog entry a <code>catalog:</code> reference points to — to the latest version of the aliased package, keeping the <code>npm:<name>@</code> prefix in the rewritten specifier. Previously the alias name itself was looked up on the registry, failing the update with a 404 when no package of that name exists.</p> </li> </ul>
